trip.title: Lycia by Fire & Sea
trip.intro: A coast of warm water, pine forests, mountain ruins and fire that has burned since antiquity.

locations.name: Çamyuva
locations.note: Pine-shaded base with the mountains at your back and the sea in front.
locations.description: This is the deliberate compromise pin for the trip: close to Phaselis, close enough to Kemer for dinner, and quieter than the main resort strip.
details: Use Çamyuva or nearby Kiriş as the base for the full trip.
A hire car makes the early trailheads and sunset drives much easier.
The coast road and dolmuş network are useful for shorter hops.

locations.name: Phaselis
locations.note: Three ancient harbours and a pine forest full of ruins. Swim when the walking wins.
locations.description: Founded by Rhodians around 690 BC, Phaselis was a trading port with three harbours. Its ruins now run through pine forest and down to clear swimming coves.
details: Allow half a day for the main street, aqueduct and harbours.
Bring swim shoes and water: shade is generous, services less so.
A good low-effort day when the family wants history and sea together.

locations.name: Tahtalı Dağı
locations.note: Cable car from 726 m to 2,365 m in about ten minutes.
locations.description: The Lycian Olympus is the trip’s big altitude change: a cable-car summit with huge views over the coast and a sharp drop in temperature from the beach.
details: Take a warm layer and windproof shell even on a hot beach day.
The summit station reaches 2,365 m; conditions can change quickly.
Use the cable car for the view, or make the ascent a serious walking day.

locations.name: Yanartaş
locations.note: Methane-rich flames burning from bare rock since antiquity — go at dusk.
locations.description: Yanartaş means ‘burning stone’. Methane and hydrogen seep through fractured rock, creating dozens of flames that gave rise to the Greek story of the Chimera.
details: The path climbs over rough stone; proper shoes and a headtorch matter.
Dusk makes the flames most atmospheric, but plan the descent before it is fully dark.
A ruined Temple of Hephaestus sits below the vents.

locations.name: Olympos
locations.note: A ruined city swallowed by forest, ending on a long shingle beach.
locations.description: Once a major Lycian League city, Olympos later became associated with piracy. Today the path through the ruins ends at a broad beach shared with Çıralı.
details: Pair the ruins with a swim and a walk along the protected beach.
The river corridor is shady and atmospheric but uneven underfoot.
It works naturally as the landward half of a Çıralı day.

locations.name: Adrasan
locations.note: Quiet bay and the start of the Musa Dağı crossing to Olympos.
locations.description: Adrasan is a calmer southern bay and a useful marker for the longer Lycian Way terrain beyond Olympos.
details: Treat the Musa Dağı crossing as a proper full-day hike, not a casual walk.
The bay itself is the softer option if the trail weather turns.
Carry water: services thin out quickly once you leave the coast.

locations.name: Göynük Canyon
locations.note: Clear-water gorge; the lower canyon is family-sized, the uplands are serious hiking.
locations.description: The lower gorge offers pools, waterfalls and a manageable adventure day. Above it, the Lycian Way quickly becomes rougher and more remote.
details: Water shoes and a dry bag are useful for the wet sections.
Keep the lower canyon as the family default; do not underestimate the upper route.
Combine it with Kemer or a short coastal afternoon rather than overloading the day.

locations.name: Termessos
locations.note: A mountain city Alexander failed to force; its ruins remain largely unexcavated.
locations.description: Termessos sits around 1,000 m in the forested Taurus foothills. Its defensive position was strong enough that Alexander the Great moved on rather than take it.
details: This is the toughest archaeological visit: uneven paths, steps and a mountain approach.
The theatre is the defining view, but allow time for the cemetery and city walls.
Go early for cooler temperatures and a quieter site.

locations.name: Antalya · Kaleiçi
locations.note: Ottoman harbour quarter, Hadrian’s Gate and the Karaalioğlu clifftop park.
locations.description: Antalya’s old town is the urban counterpoint to the coast days: Ottoman lanes, a Roman gate, a historic harbour and high cliffs above the Mediterranean.
details: Use the old town for a flexible arrival or departure day.
Start at Hadrian’s Gate, then drift downhill towards the harbour.
Karaalioğlu Park gives the best easy sunset pause above the water.
